statement: This record remains negative evidence on build 26200.8246: the repo did not produce enough supporting proof to promote it into a normal actionable surface.

anticheat_risk.anticheat_details: DPC watchdog profiling thresholds influence kernel watchdog/profile behavior and should be reviewed before use on anti-cheat or DRM-protected systems.

gating_reason: Cross-layer evidence is strong, but an explicit policy or supportability gate still blocks promotion.

links.title: Repo system docs list explicit DpcWatchdogProfile defaults
links.summary: Repo docs list `DpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes = 266240`, `DpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThreshold = 110000`, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset = 10000`, and `DpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThreshold = 18333` under `Session Manager\\Kernel`.

links.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD bundle reads live DPC watchdog profile globals
links.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD bundle resolved the current-build `KeDpcWatchdogProfile*` symbol cluster and directly read `OffsetMs = 10000`, `SingleDpcThresholdMs = 0`, `CumulativeDpcThresholdMs = 0`, `BufferSizeBytes = 0`, plus control `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0`.

links.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly shows DPC watchdog reader and validator path
links.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` directly reads the profile and control watchdog globals and only sets output bits / copies values when the globals are non-zero, while `KiValidateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` backfills missing fields from the same globals and validates range constraints.

links.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly excludes KiApplyProcessorDpcLimits as seeding caller
links.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KiApplyProcessorDpcLimits` forwards an input configuration block to `KiSetProcessorDpcLimits` and does not directly read the watchdog profile globals.

links.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly excludes KiSetProcessorDpcLimits as seeding caller
links.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KiSetProcessorDpcLimits` copies a prepared watchdog configuration block into per-processor state but does not directly read the watchdog profile globals.

links.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly shows explicit DPC watchdog writer path
links.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` validates caller input, writes the DPC watchdog globals under lock, applies the profile-buffer fallback, and then calls `KiCreateDpcLimitsProcessorConfiguration` to build the per-processor limits block.
